AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to designating the state and

form distribution and assistance, and permitting independent institutions of

items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1128

SPONSOR: BENJAMIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the election law, in relation to designating the state
and city universities of New York as participating agencies for voter
registration form distribution and assistance, and permitting independ-
ent institutions of higher education to do the same upon request

 
PURPOSE:

To require the State and City Universities of New York (SUNY and CUNY)
and any other College or University that chooses to participate, to
provide voter registration forms and absentee ballots upon requests.
And for these locations to assist in completion of these documents.
These locations will also have the Proper documents when needed for a
change of address.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: amends the opening paragraph of section 5-211 of the election
law to include SUNY, CUNY and participating schools as additional
locations providing voter registration forms.

Section 2: amends subdivision 4 of section 5-211 of the election law to
include SUNY, CUNY and participating schools as additional locations
providing absentee ballot forms.

 
EXISTING LAW:

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Chapter 659 of the laws of 1994 is commonly referred to as the "Motor
Voter" law. "Motor-Voter" is credited for registering 315,778 new votes
for 1995. However, of the 16 participating agencies, none specifically
served or targeted young voters. Individuals, aged 18 to 30, have been
labeled "Generation H. Unfortunately the original Motor-Voter bill
passed by the legislature fell short of delivering Motor-Voter access
for many of this age group. Many 18 to 30 year old students are enrolled
in some part of the New York State higher education system.

These students are not a special interest group, nor do they desire to
become one. This bill would include SUNY and CUNY as "Motor-Voter" agen-
cies. SUNY and CUNY are "taxpayer funded", no different than the current
16 "Motor-voter" agencies. The State has a responsibility to encourage
participation in the electoral process.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017-18: S.2316
2015-16: S.4802
2013-14: S.1803/A.456
2011-12: S.3879/A813

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect after 120 days.

AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to voter registration form

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1128A

SPONSOR: BENJAMIN
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the election law, in relation to voter
registration form distribution and assistance

 
PURPOSE:

To require the State and City Universities of New York (SUNY and CUNY)
to provide voter registration forms and absentee ballots to students,
and for these locations to assist in completion of these documents.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1: amends the opening paragraph of section 5-211 of the election
law to update references to the Office for People With Developmental
Disabilities, district offices of the Workers' Compensation Board, and
United States Citizenship and Immigration Services.

Section 2: adds anew subdivision 18 of section 5-211 of the election law
to include SUNY and CUNY as additional locations providing voter regis-
tration forms and absentee ballot forms, and to require SUNY and CUNY to
submit annual compliance reports to the State Board of Elections.

Section 3: provides an effective date.

 
EXISTING LAW:

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Chapter 659 of the laws of 1994 is commonly referred to as the "Motor
Voter" law. "Motor-Voter" is credited for registering 315,778 new votes
for 1995. However, of the 16 participating agencies, none specifically
served or targeted young voters. Unfortunately the original Motor-Voter
bill passed by the legislature fell short of delivering Motor-Voter
access for many of this age group.

Many 18 to 30 year old students are enrolled in some part of the New
York State higher education system. These students are not a special
interest group, nor, do they desire to become one. This bill would
include SUNY and CUNY as "Motor-Voter" agencies. SUNY and CUNY are
"taxpayer funded", no different than the current 16 "Motor-Voter" agen-
cies. The State has a responsibility to encourage participation in the
electoral process. (Sponsor)

State law requires SUNY and CUNY campuses to provide all students with
voter registration forms at the beginning of each school year, as well
as in January of each Presidential election year. Federal law also
mandates that these institutions provide students an opportunity to
register to vote, as well as assistance and filing of registration
forms. Data from the last few years has shown that voter registration
rates at many of New York's public colleges are lagging behind other
higher education institutions nationally.

In July 2017, Governor Cuomo ordered SUNY and CUNY to conduct a full
investigation of their voter registration practices in order to ensure
that required steps are being taken to increase voter registration rates
among voters on New York's public college campuses, and to develop plans
to educate students of their rights and ensure administrators are meet-
ing legal obligations. To date, the results of those investigations and
plans are not readily available for each university system and campus.
Requiring each campus to submit annual reports will increase transparen-
cy and accountability.  (Governor Cuomo's July 24, 2017 letter to SUNY
and CUNY.)

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017-2018 - A.3962-A - Reported to Ways and Means
2015-16 - A.394 - Referred to Election Law
2013-14 - A.456 - Advanced to 3rd reading Cal. 94/S.1803 - Referred to
Elections

2003-04 - A.2971 - Reported to Rules
2001-02 - A.1180 - Advanced to 3rd reading, Cal. 329
1999-00 - A.1993 - Referred to Election Law

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

minimal

 
LOCAL FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

none

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 30 Chapter 587
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 1128-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the election law, in relation to voter registration
        form distribution and assistance"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  vital legislation will help ensure robust voter participation by
students enrolled in universities throughout New York State. It requires
the State and City Universities of New York to provide additional  voter
registration  information  to  students  at the beginning of each school
year, as well as in  January  of  a  Presidential  election  year.  This
includes  building  an educational website and providing voter registra-
tion forms and absentee ballots  via  email.  Finally,  the  legislation
requires  annual  reporting  of  voter registration efforts to the State
Board of Elections.
 
  However, the original version of this legislation placed a significant
operational burden on  the  University  system.  Additionally,  language
needed to be fixed to provide clarity as to when absentee ballots should
be distributed, and how data should be collected and reported.
 
  The  Executive  has agreed to sign this legislation based on an agree-
ment with the Legislature to remedy these deficiencies and provide addi-
tional time so SUNY and CUNY can work to fulfill the requirements of the
bill as swiftly as possible. This agreement also  ensures  that  student
privacy  will be protected during data collection by removing a require-
ment to collect the number of times students click on a link  to  access
voter registration materials, and further clarifies that the annual data
reporting requirement will be disaggregated by school.

  This bill is approved.                      (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______
